newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Norway in 1st gas supply contract with Italy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Norway in 1st gas supply contract with Italy.

text.p: Norway extended its reach into the European energy market on Tuesday by announcing its first gas supply contract with Italy.

The 25-year deal between Norway's Gas Negotiating Committee (GFU) and Italian gas company SNAM SpA, a subsidiary of ENI SpA ENI.M, covers deliveries of six billion cubic metres (bcm) over 25 years, or a total of 150 bcm of natural gas.
Announcing the deal, Norwegian state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said that at current prices, the overall value of the contract was about 90 billion crowns ($13.9 billion).
The agreement is the second largest single supply contract undertaken by Norway after the huge Troll sales agreement was signed with a group of European buyers in 1986.

The Scandinavian country already delivers gas to Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Austria and Spain putting it in the top five of the global league of gas exporters along with Algeria, Indonesia, the Netherlands and Russia.
It is also the second largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia, supplying nearly three million barrels per day to the international market.

"This contract will increase Norwegian gas sales by about 10 percent," a Statoil statement said. "Before the agreement, Norwegian suppliers had committed themselves to deliver 62 billion cubic metres of gas annually from the year 2000. This level will now increase to 68 billion cubic metres."
Deliveries to SNAM will begin in 2000 and reach plateau level in 2002.
The gas will be piped through the Zeepipe and NorFra trunklines from the Norwegian North Sea to Zeebrugge, Belgium, and Dunkirk, France.

The contract completes almost two years of negotiations between the GFU and SNAM. Statoil, along with Norsk Hydro ASA and Saga Petroleum ASA are permanent GFU members. The talks also included Total Norge and Mobil Exploration Norway.
Statoil said Italy was Europe's third largest gas market after Germany and Britain, consuming 53 bcm in 1995. Based on current forecasts Italian consumption is expected to reach 90 bcm in 2010.
"The country currently imports more than 60 percent of its requirements, and this proportion is rising," Statoil said.

It said Norwegian gas will have about 16 percent of the European Union market after 2000 and meet seven percent of Italian requirements in 2005. Norway's share of the Belgian, French and German gas markets will vary between 30 and 40 percent at the end of the decade. ($ = 6.453 Norwegian Crowns)
